purpose: Revision-pinned provenance and recorded-measurement packet for four infer-observability units distilled from CANNBot skills and a redacted engineering transcript. The packet separates software contracts from observed measurements; it does not promote one into the other.

source_snapshot.privacy: Absolute workspace paths, hostnames, container identifiers, usernames and internal endpoints are omitted.

claims: Task Start Time, Task Duration and Task Wait Time are distinct columns; Task Wait Time is not part of Task Duration.
aic_mac_ratio, aiv_vec_ratio, aic_mte2_ratio, aiv_mte2_ratio and aiv_mte3_ratio are 0-1 cycle-share ratios, not wall-clock percentages.
Task Type determines which AIC/AIV columns are meaningful; a blank or 0 value is not by itself proof of a zero measurement.
Task Duration(us) is the core per-task time metric; Block Dim and Mix Block Dim are launch-shape fields.
Pipe ratios are per-core row values; the reference gives producer-side interpretation thresholds, not universal pass/fail laws.
Memory fields expose transfer paths separately from pipe-cycle ratios.
The standard comparable protocol uses adjacent warmup -> target pairs, excludes warmup from total_us, and takes the median of ten target sums.
Native msprof supports one --aic-metrics group per run; op_summary_*.csv is a per-op aggregate rather than per-core data.
Per-core analysis requires the sample-based aicore.db path; warmup is mandatory to avoid DVFS and first-run effects.
Level1 plus PipeUtilization supplies the detailed 47-column kernel_details view; without ExperimentalConfig only about nine columns remain.
The profiler schedule must leave the active window; prof.step() calls must cover skip_first + warmup + active plus a closing step.
Graph compile/JIT must be warmed outside the capture window; prefill and decode should be captured separately when the question is TTFT or TPOT.
The published capture patterns place torch.npu.synchronize() after the timed work and before prof.step().
step_trace_time.csv carries Computing, Communication(Not Overlapped), Overlapped, Communication, Free, Stage, Bubble, Preparing and a related exclude-receive field.
These are separate columns, so a step budget must preserve the overlap term rather than adding Communication and Computing directly.
High Task Wait Time is a scheduling/overlap symptom, not a kernel-execution-time proof.
Weak aic_mac_ratio or low cube utilization suggests poor tile feeding; high MTE ratios suggest movement pressure.
The reference explicitly separates op_summary interpretation from task_time gap analysis and api_statistic host overhead.
asys collect and asys launch produce {output}/asys_output_timestamp; asys analyze produces the same shape and reports the info.txt path.
asys is EP-only; collection must not be parallelized and environment variables must match the service runtime.
Device firmware logs, stackcore and coretrace have privilege and product-support constraints.
The aicore_error triggers are 'there is an aivec error exception' and 'there is an aicore error exception'.
asys analyze -r=aicore_error accepts a collected path or auto-collects; it analyzes only the first AI Core Error in log time order.
The output info.txt is the analysis entry point, and --output must not be nested inside --path.
msaicerr is local-only, needs Python 3.7.5+, is not supported on RC, and must run from its own tool directory.
-p selects the fault-information directory; -out must be a disjoint path and must not be inside -p.
The tool parses the first AI Core Error by log time; info.txt is the result and debug_info.txt is the tool log.
The collection must contain dfx/data-dump, dfx/ops .o/.json artifacts, and dfx/log/host/cann logs; missing elements block extraction.
The command form is python3 msaicerr.py -p <collect> -out <result> -dev <device>; -out may not be inside -p.
The recommended order is unsupported-op gate, three-element check, disjoint paths, info.txt, then debug_info.txt if the tool itself fails.
msnpureport exports device-side logs and DFX data; report, config --get and config --set are distinct entry points.
Export and config --set operations have privilege and product-form constraints; -d uses logical IDs, not the physical IDs shown by npu-smi.
stackcore and ub_info outputs are parsed by asys, which is the downstream analysis tool.
The workflow runs Phase 0 through Phase 5 locally, with input checks, three-element validation, scene classification, msaicerr analysis, register decoding, reproduction and evidence-chain reporting.
A missing plog is a stop condition; missing dump or .o/.json lowers confidence but may allow a constructed-data path.
Register decode, dump validation, disassembly and single-op reproduction are separate evidence chains and must not be collapsed.
info.txt has six sections; the third section reports Original Info and, when available, Corrected Info with start pc, current pc and an estimated assembly offset.
Corrected Info is preferred because it is backfilled from AI Core error registers; the offset is an estimate, not a source line.
The objdump fallback resolves the offset to a cce line and then through _loc.json to a TBE source line; L0 stops at the assembly offset.
Dump failure has three concrete signatures: dump callback failure, D2H failure and invalid address.
Chip dialect must be decided before decoding: hexadecimal error codes point to Stars/910B, decimal bit lists to David/950, and a bare 0 is ambiguous.
The high-frequency bit table gives concrete Stars and David bit names for OOB reads, UB overflow/wrap, atomic errors and INF/NaN inputs.
The six *_ERR_INFO subregisters have unit-specific bit fields; David has no subregister decode and uses error-name prefixes instead.
No error bit set produces trap_or_timeout, which is a fallback and not proof of a confirmed timeout; conclusion codes 101-107 are separate from tool status codes.
npu-objdump or msobjdump supports dump-elf, list-elf, extract-elf and, only when detected, sass.
Inputs include standalone device ELF, fused host ELF with .aicore_binary, static libraries and supported .ascend.kernel packages; format is detected from content, not extension.
sass means Ascend AICore instructions; the disassembly backend is a CANN llvm-objdump with the Ascend target, not a host GNU objdump.
The workflow records the actual metadata and instruction-disassembly tools, selects the exact object by runtime identity/SHA256, and chooses _mix_aic or _mix_aiv from the exception core type.
ERR_INFO PC rules are unit-specific: CCU bits[30:23]||[7:0], MTE/VEC bits[39:32]||[7:0], CUBE bits[31:24]||[7:0], IFU whole value; the 16-bit instruction address is multiplied by 4.
Decoded PC and current_pc - start_pc are comparable only in the same byte-address domain; an object-relative offset needs a matching base.
A narrow instruction window must contain the target instruction; disassembly alone does not prove runtime load identity or root cause.
Public error-code documentation proves public semantics and user guidance, not target-version registration or execution.
Four evidence layers are separate: public catalog, target-version registration, target build include chain, and negative runtime behavior.
A code being documented must not be read as 'registered and callable in this build'.
E*9*** is an internal-code pattern, not a semantic code for new development; generic internal codes must not be used as a fallback.
The root-cause layer reports once; outer layers add PLOG context and pass the original return through.
When a lower layer already reported a concrete error, adding EZ9999 is duplicate reporting and must not be treated as the root cause.
EI0006 is the HCCL communication error 'Getting socket times out'; its Reason field identifies srcRank/dstRank and the recommended checks.
EL0004 is the driver memory-allocation failure 'Failed to allocate memory'; the documented cause is insufficient memory and the suggested action is to close unused applications.
EZ9999 is not present in this documented catalog; a full-file search found no EZ9999 entry.
source_records.scope_note: Line ranges are JSON entry locators because the file is machine-readable; the SHA256 is over the complete file.

claims: op_common::OP_LOGE and several wrapper macros commonly end at EZ9999; the audit must inspect the actual macro and REPORT_INNER_ERR_MSG leaf.
EZ9999 is a generalized internal code and must be reclassified by actual root cause; it is not a precise fault category.
Detection of an internal code authorizes review, not mechanical replacement with another code.
ACLNN_ERR_INNER*, ACL_ERROR_FAILURE and 5-prefixed errors map statically to EZ9999 and must be reclassified by root cause.
Static mapping is an audit aid; the target-version implementation remains authoritative.
507035 is the ACL/RT vector-core exception, usually raised through aclrtStreamSynchronize.
Typical causes are UB-side 32-byte misalignment, GM-to-UB padParams violations, or UB overflow.
507035 is distinct from 507046 stream-sync timeout.
The 507035 checklist checks UB-side DataCopy/DataCopyPad start addresses, VEC operand starts, blockLen units and padParams, dynamic chunk alignment, tmpBuf sizing and total UB usage.
blockLen itself has no 32-byte alignment requirement; the 32-byte constraint is on the UB-side address, and padParams left/right padding is limited to 32 bytes.
507035 is a runtime signal; it is not by itself a specific aic_error bit.
Observed AICPU failure signature: 'AICPU error: errorCode=0x2a, taskid: 1, retcode: 507018'.
The same experience page also records 'aicore error (507018 / 0x2a)' when a heavy loop is expanded in Python rather than emitted as a device loop.
These are experience reports, not a universal mapping; 507018 should be treated as an AICPU/task-side exception and confirmed from the first plog line.
The LLM graph-mode guide identifies memory-address changes, shape changes, Python control flow and .item() as the main causes of graph break or recompilation.
A .item() in forward converts a Tensor to a Python scalar and forces a graph break; the recommended pattern is a static parameter or a precomputed value.
Recompilation is diagnosed with torch._logging.set_logs(recompiles=True); dynamic=False plus guard settings are the next checks.
npugraph_ex uses capture-and-replay (aclgraph); GE converts the FX graph to Ascend IR, so replay evidence differs by backend.
Forward code must not use .item(); fixed tensors are created outside the graph and marked static.
The troubleshooting order is aot_eager, force_eager, then graph-mode recompile or graph-break analysis.
Collective cost must be split into wait-caused high duration and real transfer/link bottlenecks.
Wait diagnosis uses Notify Wait and cross-rank same-op alignment; a single rank's communication time cannot establish low bandwidth.
The gate is explicit: if wait-caused, stop before retry/relay/bandwidth conclusions; if insufficient evidence, state the missing tables or fields.

observed_measurements.scope: One successful engine-0 request, 158 generation tokens, before the concurrent C128 phase.
observed_measurements.interpretation: A single-request baseline: TTFT about 1.26 s and TPOT about 14.9 ms on this engine.
observed_measurements.limits: This is one request on one engine; it does not establish a fleet baseline or a percentile.

observed_measurements.scope: Engine 0 after a 128-concurrency phase; 32 successful requests on this engine, 129 successful requests across four engines.
observed_measurements.interpretation: At high concurrency, queueing moves mean TTFT to about 76 s and mean TPOT to about 700 ms on the same engine.
observed_measurements.limits: This is not a clean regression against the single-request run: concurrency, batching and queueing differ. It demonstrates why the load protocol must be matched before comparing TTFT or TPOT.

observed_measurements.scope: Rank 0, three intermediate decode steps, 128K input and 1K output, TP8/DP4/EP32/DCP1 with MLA DSpark3.
observed_measurements.interpretation: The observed identity is Stage = Computing + Communication - Overlapped + Free. This window is communication-dominated, but single-rank Communication includes wait and is not a bandwidth proof.
observed_measurements.limits: Profiling overhead is inside the window; the report explicitly warns that this is not an unprofiled steady-state TPOT.

observed_measurements.scope: Five adjacent steps from one small operator-chain capture.
observed_measurements.interpretation: Computing is nearly flat while Free varies by about 10x, so aggregate wall time is dominated by per-step host/launch gaps in this sample.
observed_measurements.limits: Five steps from one capture; it is an illustration of the field, not a general host-overhead law.

observed_measurements.scope: Two adjacent rows in a real PipeUtilization export from one MIX_AIC workload.
observed_measurements.interpretation: Task Wait Time can be hundreds of times Task Duration. For MlaPrologV3 the device row is only about 53 us while the wait column is about 1.65 ms; for Muls the wait is about 5.3 ms against a 14 us duration. Those waits are scheduling/queue evidence, not kernel execution.
observed_measurements.limits: The wait column's exact queue semantics depend on the exporter; use it as a scheduling signal and corroborate with task_time/trace gaps.

observed_measurements.scope: msprof summary for one MlaPrologV3 row.
observed_measurements.interpretation: The head overhead is small here; MTE2 is the largest AIC pipe ratio while MAC ratio is only about 26%, so a high cube_utilization number must not be read as a high MAC share.
observed_measurements.limits: A single row; use the per-pipe ratios and the actual shape/tiling before declaring a bound.

observed_measurements.scope: TP8/DP8/EP64/DCP8 serving run with GQA DSpark7 and EPLB policy3; two profiler-stop windows and three throughput-zero windows.
observed_measurements.interpretation: Profiler stop/parse and an EPLB Queue.get path can both create multi-second forward stalls while requests remain running. Graph replay counts were present, so a graph-out small op alone does not prove a full eager fallback.
observed_measurements.limits: The 45/56 s are stop_profile request durations, not per-token ITL. The 1225 ms and 7-9 ms are a constructed A/B, not a whole-service ITL gain.

observed_measurements.scope: One four-node serving startup; first effective error before graph capture.
observed_measurements.interpretation: 507018 appeared as an AICPU/task-side exception in a collective launch, not as a proven timeout. The first error must be read from the lower-level AICPU line rather than inferred from the ACL return code.
observed_measurements.limits: One incident; the 0x2a mapping is not universal across CANN/SoC versions.

observed_measurements.scope: Two adjacent rank-0 profiling windows covering 50 decode steps.
observed_measurements.interpretation: The captured steps show graph replay calls at the expected main+draft rate; metadata/sampling/logits matmul outside the graph do not by themselves prove a whole-model fallback.
observed_measurements.limits: The windows cover about six seconds; absence of fallback there does not prove absence elsewhere.

EZ9999.meaning: A generalized internal code emitted by wrappers such as op_common::OP_LOGE; it is not a precise root cause.
EZ9999.action: Find the lower-level EE/EI/EL or first [ERROR] line; do not add another EZ9999 or treat it as the root cause.

EL0004.meaning: Failed to allocate memory; documented cause is insufficient memory.
EL0004.action: Check HBM/free memory, process footprint, allocator/OOM evidence and npu-smi; do not attribute to a kernel OOB without address evidence.

EI0006.meaning: Getting socket times out; the Reason field names srcRank/dstRank and the recommended checks.
EI0006.action: Read the Reason, compare both endpoints, check process liveness and network reachability; redact endpoints in reports.

507015.meaning: An ACL/RT surface for an AI Core exception; not the fault bitmask.
507015.action: Route to the first plog AI Core Error line and msaicerr; do not stop at the return code.

507018.surface: AICPU/task-side exception; observed with AICPU errorCode=0x2a and ACL 507018 / 0x715002a.
507018.meaning: An AICPU or task execution failure; not by itself a timeout and not a specific AICore arithmetic bit.
507018.action: Read the first AICPU line, identify the task/kernel and collective, and check both the AICPU launch and the downstream ACL surface.

507035.surface: ACL/RT vector-core exception, usually reported by aclrtStreamSynchronize.
507035.meaning: A runtime signal for a vector-core fault; common causes are UB-side 32-byte misalignment, padParams violations and UB overflow.
507035.action: Run the UB alignment/overflow checklist; do not invent a single aic_error bit for it.

candidate_bits.name: mte_biu_rdwr_resp
candidate_bits.meaning: MTE access to an invalid GM address or cross-device timeout

candidate_bits.name: mte_gdma_read_overflow
candidate_bits.meaning: MTE instruction reads an on-chip buffer out of bounds

candidate_bits.name: biu_l2_read_oob
candidate_bits.meaning: bus read OOB; check L2-side access

candidate_bits.name: MTE_BIU_RDWR_RESP
candidate_bits.meaning: invalid GM access or cross-device timeout

candidate_bits.name: MTE_GDMA_READ_OVERFLOW
candidate_bits.meaning: MTE2 read UB / MTE3 read L1-UB out of bounds

mte2_oob_gm_read.corroboration: GM address, transfer length, allocation range, LD/ST instruction, dump tensor bounds; a single bit does not prove the exact buffer.

candidate_bits.name: MTE_ATM_ADD_ADDR_MISALIGN
candidate_bits.meaning: MTE atomic instruction address is not aligned; atomic-only

ub_unaligned.runtime_signature: 507035 vector-core exception is the usual surface for a UB-side 32-byte misalignment or overflow; it is not a single stable aic_error bit.
ub_unaligned.corroboration: UB-side DataCopy/DataCopyPad start address, VEC operand start, dynamic chunk alignment, blockLen bytes, padParams, total UB usage.

candidate_bits.name: vec_idata_inf_nan
candidate_bits.meaning: instruction input is INF or NAN

candidate_bits.name: cube_invld_input
candidate_bits.meaning: L0A/L0B data is INF or NAN

candidate_bits.name: VEC_ERR_IDATA_INF_NAN_T0
candidate_bits.meaning: instruction input is INF or NAN

candidate_bits.name: CUBE_INVLD_INPUT
candidate_bits.meaning: L0A/L0B data is INF or NAN

vector_nan_inf.corroboration: Dump NaN/INF check, input value range, upstream producer; the bit identifies the unit, not which input tensor is bad.

queue_deadlock.runtime_signature: No dedicated aic_error bit. Suspect no-progress plus 507014 aicore timeout, fftsplus task execute failed, or trap_or_timeout when no bit is set.
queue_deadlock.corroboration: set_flag/wait_flag pairing, stream/task dependency graph, collective ordering across ranks, task/stream IDs, and whether the first error is elsewhere.
queue_deadlock.warning: trap_or_timeout is the no-bit fallback and must not be read as a confirmed queue deadlock.

excluded: container identifiers and private service directories
redaction.method: Only relative artifact locators, SHA256 digests and numeric/structural observations are retained. Quoted log semantics are paraphrased rather than copied with endpoints.
redaction.verification: Manual scan of the packet and all four units for IP literals, absolute user-home paths and account names before index rebuild.

limitations: The CANNBot documents are community/ecosystem software contracts, not target-version runtime registration proof.
RTS codes are ACL/RT surface codes; their exact lower-level cause depends on CANN, driver and SoC version.
The observed measurements come from several different runs and parallelism settings; they illustrate field behaviour and are not a controlled A/B.
reproduced_empirical in the dependent unit refers to the recorded runs in this packet; this distillation did not execute new NPU work.
No observed value here establishes a universal performance threshold or a hardware defect rate.
